title.en: CF packed fields: mask before scale, preserve coordinates

summary: Validate CF-NetCDF missing-value decoding and coordinate metadata before constructing a scalar field or time sequence.
objective: Decode a packed CF field with fill values and nontrivial coordinate variables, then verify probes show only valid physical values at their declared locations.
intent_signals: Decode a packed CF field with fill values and nontrivial coordinate variables, then verify probes show only valid physical values at their declared locations.
example_prompts: Decode a packed CF field with fill values and nontrivial coordinate variables, then verify probes show only valid physical values at their declared locations.
applies_when: Validate CF-NetCDF missing-value decoding and coordinate metadata before constructing a scalar field or time sequence.

principles: Distinguish stored packed numbers, valid decoded quantities and display colors. Missing data must not become a real extreme value or zero sample.
Keep dimensions, coordinate variables, units and time metadata attached to each selected field. An array axis called x is not enough to establish a geographic position.
implementation: Record whether the reader already applied masking/scaling. With raw packed input, evaluate missing and valid-range metadata in the packed domain, mask invalid samples, then scale valid values and add offset once. Never repeat decoding on an already-decoded array.
Use decoded units for probes and legends; preserve the raw representation and decoding metadata for inspection. Exclude masked samples from displayed extrema and show an all-missing field explicitly.

Resolve dimensions and any auxiliary coordinates/grid mapping instead of assuming evenly spaced Cartesian indices. Preserve the supplied time unit/calendar, and report unsupported calendars or coordinates before labeling a timeline or geographic view.

Limit this bridge to the supported regular/explicit-coordinate array representation. Reject unsupported gathering, mesh topology or coordinate-subsampling encodings rather than reshaping them into a regular grid.
observable_checks: With raw values [-32768,0,100], fill=-32768, scale=0.1 and offset=273.15, show missing, 273.15 and 283.15 in declared decoded units; the fill value never affects the legend range.
Pass the already-decoded values through the display bridge: they remain unchanged and are not scaled a second time.

Use equal array dimensions with different coordinate values; locations follow coordinates. An all-missing field shows no invented zero-valued surface, and unsupported time metadata produces an explicit limitation.

known_limits: Decoding does not validate forecast quality, conservation, observation calibration or uncertainty. Reprojection and numerical resampling need separately verified methods.
Authored source-reviewed guidance only; no import adapter, runtime artifact or scientific pipeline was implemented or executed.
creative_affordances: Use a compact source-versus-display inspector to expose the specific transformation; layout and emphasis are authored choices, not validated usability findings.

claims.statement: CF 1.12 treats missing/valid-range indicators for packed variables in the external packed domain and requires valid-value checks before scaling; decoding multiplies by scale_factor before adding add_offset, with units describing unpacked values.
claims.scope: CF 1.12 sections 2.5.1 and 8.1; application decoding state must prevent double application.

source_refs.locator: 2.5.1 Missing data, valid and actual range of data; 8.1 Packed Data

claims.statement: CF associates field dimensions with coordinate variables and supports auxiliary coordinate variables identified by the coordinates attribute; grid mapping metadata can supply geographic interpretation.
claims.scope: CF 1.12 sections 5, 5.2 and 5.6; not a projection implementation.

source_refs.locator: 5 Coordinate Systems and Domain; 5.2 Two-Dimensional Latitude, Longitude Coordinate Variables; 5.6 Horizontal Coordinate Reference Systems, Grid Mappings, and Projections
